business.text: a subscription for one physical thing

audience.firstUsers: Partner with one college's first-gen student society and run a launch session with them.

audience.text: for people who just moved cities
audience.firstUsers: Post in 'new to [your city]' groups on Reddit and Facebook.

money.n: hospitals and warehouses pay per worker

audience.firstUsers: Hand out flyers at a hospital or warehouse gate during the 7 a.m. shift change.
Visit three hostels near campus and set it up for one warden for free.
Run a free 'phone help' morning at a senior center.
Find resellers on Instagram and offer them a free month.

money.n: priced below one plate a day

audience.firstUsers: Pick one busy food street and sign vendors up in person.
Message 30 wedding DJs on Instagram with a 60-second demo.
Talk to riders waiting outside busy restaurants at lunchtime.

audience.text: for people who kill every plant
audience.firstUsers: Start a 'my plant graveyard' photo trend on Instagram.

money.n: event hosts pay for better mixers

audience.firstUsers: Partner with one meetup organizer and run it at their next event.
Post in r/Cubers and show up at your next local competition.
Ask your own landlord. Awkward, but fast.

twist.text: where you pay what you think it was worth, afterwards
where every new feature is voted in by users each week
that sends a paper postcard every month
where you can only post from the exact location
with a human double-checking every answer
that only works when two people press the button together
where the AI argues against you first
that deletes itself unless someone vouches for it
with a physical button you stick on the fridge
that gets worse the more you use it

money.n: pay to make it good again

twist.text: where strangers can only reply with one emoji
where your mom is the admin
that only unlocks during a full moon

auction.n: a small cut when the lowest bid wins

bounty.n: a share of each paid bounty

capsule.n: a physical copy on opening day

auction: A request form: what you need, budget and deadline
Sellers bid down against a countdown
Pick a winner and pay through the site
bounty: Post a task with a reward and a deadline
People claim it and submit proof
Hold the reward with a payment provider and release it on approval
bot: A WhatsApp Business number that does one clear job
Simple menu replies before any AI
matchmaker: Matching rules you can explain in one sentence
An intro message that makes the first chat easy
sticker: Unique QR codes printed on stickers
A scan page that reaches the owner without revealing them
An owner dashboard for their tagged things
extension: A browser extension that does one thing on one website
Publish on the Chrome Web Store
subscription: A landing page with one product and one price
A shipping sheet you can fulfil from home at first
club: A monthly cap on new members
hotline: A phone number from a calling API
A voice menu with three options
capsule: Write, record or upload something to seal
An email and a printable card on opening day
leaderboard: One metric people can log honestly
A reset every season to keep it fair
pet: A creature whose mood follows one real habit
A daily check-in that feeds it
hardware: A QR or UPI payment code on the front
show: A pilot episode shot on a phone
Audience voting on the next episode

daily.title: Pay a local student to video-check a flat before you rent it
daily.pitch: Moving to a new city? A verified student near the flat does a live video walkthrough with your checklist, so you don't sign blind.
daily.problem: People relocating for college or a job rent flats from photos, then discover damp walls, weak water pressure or a 40-minute walk to the metro.
daily.whoPays: People relocating to a new city; relocation teams at companies.
mvp: Request form with the listing link and your checklist
Match a verified student within 3 km
Live video call with the checklist on screen
Short photo report after the call
daily.firstUsers: Post in 'moving to [city]' groups and pay the first ten walkers yourself to prove it works.

daily.title: A vault that hands your 'if something happens' notes to one person
daily.pitch: Write down where the important stuff is. If you stop checking in for 60 days, one trusted person gets it.
daily.problem: After an accident or a death, families scramble because nobody knows which bank, which insurer or which password manager to look in.
daily.whoPays: Adults with families or dependents; insurers can offer it as a perk.
mvp: Monthly one-tap check-in by email or WhatsApp
One trusted contact with a calm release message
A grace period with reminders before anything is sent
daily.firstUsers: Publish a genuinely useful 'what my family would need' checklist; the vault is the obvious next step for readers.

daily.title: Rehearsal coach for wedding toasts and farewell speeches
daily.pitch: Record your speech and get feedback on length, pace, jokes that won't land and names you mispronounce, then practice until it's good.
daily.problem: Best men and maids of honor write speeches the night before, run long, and bomb in front of 300 people.
daily.whoPays: Anyone giving a speech soon; wedding planners bundle it.
daily.pricing: $9 per speech, with unlimited rehearsals for two weeks.
mvp: Flags for inside jokes and risky lines
daily.firstUsers: Partner with two wedding planners and offer it free to the speakers at their next five weddings.

daily.title: Turn your grocery receipt into this week's dinners
daily.pitch: Snap the receipt and get five dinners that use what you bought, ordered by what spoils first.
daily.problem: People buy vegetables with good intentions and throw a third of them away by Friday.
daily.whoPays: Home cooks on a freemium plan; grocery chains pay to feature it at checkout.
daily.pricing: Free for two receipts a week; $2 per month unlimited.
mvp: Recipes ranked by what expires first
daily.firstUsers: Post before-and-after 'food I wasted this week' photos in budget-cooking communities.

daily.title: Polite notes between neighbors, without the awkward knock
daily.pitch: A QR code in the lobby lets neighbors send short, anonymous, pre-worded notes like 'music after midnight' or 'your car blocks mine'.
daily.problem: Small annoyances in apartment buildings turn into feuds because nobody wants to knock on a stranger's door.
daily.whoPays: Housing societies and building managers.
mvp: Flat-to-flat notes with preset polite wording
Rate limits so it can't be used to harass
daily.firstUsers: Put it up in your own building with the society's permission and share the results in local groups.

daily.title: Photo menus in eight languages for local restaurants
daily.pitch: Tourists scan a QR code and see every dish with a photo, a plain description and allergy tags in their own language.
daily.problem: Tourists skip great local restaurants because they can't read the menu and are too shy to ask.
daily.whoPays: Restaurants in tourist areas.
daily.pricing: $19 per month per restaurant; photos shot on your first visit.
mvp: Photograph each dish with a phone
AI translation checked by a native speaker
Language picker on the QR page
daily.firstUsers: Walk the busiest tourist street in your city and offer three restaurants a free month.

daily.title: Fix-it club: one monthly visit that clears your list of small repairs
daily.pitch: Members add broken things to a shared list; once a month a handyperson comes and fixes all of them in one visit.
daily.problem: Renters live with dripping taps, loose handles and dead bulbs for months because each fix is too small to book someone for.
daily.whoPays: Busy renters and homeowners.
daily.pricing: $29 per month for one visit of up to 90 minutes.
mvp: A shared fix list with photos
Handyperson view with the list and parts needed
daily.firstUsers: Recruit one reliable handyperson and sell the first 20 memberships inside one apartment complex.

daily.title: 48-hour paid trial projects instead of internship interviews
daily.pitch: Small companies post a real two-day task with a fixed fee; students do it, get paid, and the best get hired.
daily.problem: Students can't prove skills without experience, and small companies waste weeks on interviews that predict nothing.
daily.whoPays: Startups and small agencies pay the trial fee plus 15%.
daily.pricing: 15% on top of each trial fee.
mvp: Company posts a scoped task and fee
Payout, plus a 'make an offer' button
daily.firstUsers: Get five founders you know to post one trial each, then share them in college placement groups.

daily.title: A tasting panel that tells restaurants if a new dish will sell
daily.pitch: Restaurants invite ten local food lovers to try a new dish for free and rate it before it goes on the menu.
daily.problem: Restaurants add dishes on a hunch and find out a month later that nobody orders them.
daily.whoPays: Restaurants and cloud kitchens.
daily.pricing: $49 per tasting; the restaurant provides the food.
mvp: Report: would order, fair price, what to fix
daily.firstUsers: Recruit 30 panelists from local food Instagram pages, then pitch three cloud kitchens.

daily.title: QR stickers that bring lost things back to you
daily.pitch: Stick one on your laptop, keys or bag. Whoever finds it scans the code and chats with you without ever seeing your number.
daily.problem: Lost-and-found runs on luck because finders have no easy, safe way to reach the owner.
daily.whoPays: Students, travelers and parents; schools buy them in bulk.
mvp: Unique codes printed on a sticker sheet
Scan page with an anonymous chat
Owner alerts on WhatsApp or email
daily.firstUsers: Sell sheets during orientation week and at your campus bookstore.

daily.title: Practice calls with an AI customer who is having a terrible day
daily.pitch: Support and sales trainees practice with realistic angry, confused or impatient AI callers and get scored on how they handled it.
daily.problem: New support staff learn to handle difficult customers on real customers, which is bad for both.
daily.whoPays: Call centers, support teams and sales bootcamps.
mvp: Five customer personas with different moods
Scorecard on tone, accuracy and resolution
Manager view of each trainee's progress
daily.firstUsers: Offer a free pilot to one call center's training batch and publish their before-and-after scores.

daily.title: One link for the office farewell gift and card
daily.pitch: Start a pot for a leaving colleague; everyone chips in and signs a shared card, and nobody chases anyone for cash.
daily.problem: Office farewells mean one person chasing 40 colleagues for money and a card that never gets signed in time.
daily.whoPays: Organizers pay a small fee; companies buy a team plan.
daily.pricing: 3% of the pot, or $10 per month for a team.
mvp: Create a pot with a deadline
Shared digital card with messages and photos
Automatic nudges to people who haven't signed
daily.firstUsers: Use it for the next farewell in your office or your parents' offices, with a small 'made with' link on the card.

daily.title: Live laundry machine status for hostels
daily.pitch: Every machine gets a QR code; students see which ones are free and get pinged when their wash is done.
daily.problem: Students carry laundry down four floors to find every machine busy, and wet clothes sit for hours after cycles end.
daily.whoPays: Hostels, PGs and laundromats.
mvp: QR per machine to start and end a cycle
A queue when every machine is busy
daily.firstUsers: Put codes on the machines in your own hostel and count how many wasted trips you save in a week.

daily.title: A rental CV that proves you're a good tenant
daily.pitch: Renters collect verified references from past landlords and flatmates into one shareable profile.
daily.problem: Good tenants get rejected or asked for huge deposits because landlords have nothing to judge them by.
daily.whoPays: Renters pay for a verified badge; landlords and brokers pay for screening.
daily.pricing: Free profile; $5 for a verified badge.
mvp: Reference requests sent to past landlords
daily.firstUsers: Target students moving into their second flat, when they finally have a landlord to vouch for them.

daily.title: Order ahead from the street stall with the longest queue
daily.pitch: Popular street food stalls take WhatsApp pre-orders with a pickup time, so regulars skip the line.
daily.problem: The best stalls lose customers at peak hours because people won't wait 30 minutes on the pavement.
daily.whoPays: Street food vendors, for less than the price of one plate a day.
mvp: WhatsApp order bot with the stall's menu
Order list on the vendor's phone
daily.firstUsers: Pick the stall with the longest queue near your college and run it for them free for a month.

daily.title: Chore auction for flatmates and families
daily.pitch: Chores go up for auction each week; whoever bids the fewest points takes the job, and points buy perks everyone agreed on.
daily.problem: Chore charts fail because nobody agrees what's fair, and the same person always ends up doing the dishes.
daily.whoPays: Households on a freemium plan.
daily.pricing: Free for one home; $2 per month for rewards and history.
mvp: Proof photo when a chore is done
A rewards shop the household sets up
daily.firstUsers: Run it in your own flat for a month and post the leaderboard; flatmate drama spreads by itself.

daily.title: Audio walking tours recorded by locals, not guidebooks
daily.pitch: Locals record 20-minute walks about their own neighborhood; visitors pay a few dollars to follow them with GPS-triggered stories.
daily.problem: Tourists see the same five landmarks, while the stories that make a neighborhood interesting live in residents' heads.
daily.whoPays: Tourists pay per walk; creators keep most of it.
mvp: Record stories pinned to map points
daily.firstUsers: Record the first three walks yourself in the old part of your city and sell them through local hostels.

daily.title: Trip deposits that make friends actually commit
daily.pitch: The group trip becomes real when everyone puts in a small deposit; whoever drops out funds the group's first dinner.
daily.problem: Group trips die in the chat because 'I'm in' costs nothing to say.
daily.whoPays: Friend groups; the organizer pays a small fee.
mvp: Trip page with dates, budget and deposit amount
Deposits held by a payment provider until the trip
daily.firstUsers: Use it for your own friends' next trip and share the page; every trip invites five to ten new people.

daily.title: A size-swap box for kids' clothes
daily.pitch: Send back what your kid has outgrown and get a box in the next size up from other families.
daily.problem: Kids outgrow clothes in months, so parents keep buying new ones while perfectly good ones sit in cupboards.
daily.whoPays: Parents of kids under eight.
mvp: Sign-up with the kid's size and style
daily.firstUsers: Run it by hand for 15 families from your local parents' group before building anything.

daily.title: Blind CV screening for small companies
daily.pitch: Upload applications and get them back with names, photos, colleges and ages removed, so the first round is about skills.
daily.problem: Small companies unintentionally filter by college name and photo, and miss great people from unknown places.
daily.whoPays: Startups and small companies hiring a few people a year.
daily.firstUsers: Offer it free to five startups that talk publicly about fair hiring.

daily.title: Before-and-after photo reports for cleaners and repair pros
daily.pitch: Cleaners, plumbers and painters send a neat photo report after each job, so landlords and clients see exactly what was done.
daily.problem: Property managers pay for work they never see, and good tradespeople can't prove they're good.
daily.whoPays: Service pros pay for pro reports; property managers pay for the dashboard.
daily.pricing: Free for five jobs a month; $9 per month after.
daily.firstUsers: Sign up five cleaners who work for short-stay rental hosts; the hosts will ask everyone else to join.
